title: Mallillin confirmed as COA chairperson by Commission on Appointments
summary: The Commission on Appointments (CA) on Monday confirmed the nomination of Commission on Audit (COA) Commissioner Douglas Michael Mallillin as the agency"s chairperson.

blocks.text: The Commission on Appointments (CA) on Monday confirmed the nomination of Commission on Audit (COA) Commissioner Douglas Michael Mallillin as the agency’s chairperson.
At a hearing, the Committee on Constitutional Commissions and Offices endorsed Mallillin’s nomination, which was confirmed by the CA in a plenary session.

Mallillin, who was appointed COA commissioner in February 2025 and confirmed in June of the same year, would serve the unexpired term of ex-COA chairperson Gamaliel Cordoba, which ends February 2, 2029.

In his opening statement, Mallillin said the chairmanship carries greater responsibility and authority to introduce reforms and innovations with technological advances, as well as to improve the government’s financial oversight.

Senator Imee Marcos initially objected to the “immediate” endorsement of Mallillin’s nomination and sought its deferment, citing concerns over the COA’s independence and the need for a clearer explanation of the nominee’s plans for the agency.
Marcos said she wanted assurances that the COA would not be used to pursue political opponents.
Mallillin committed to upholding the COA’s independence as mandated by the Constitution and said confirmation would help ensure the commission’s continued operations.
For his part, Mallillin committed to upholding the COA’s independence as mandated by the Constitution and said confirmation would help ensure the commission’s continued operations.

“We would appreciate that the nomination be confirmed so that the Commission on Audit will continue to function outside the en banc and the other functions necessary for the commission proper,” he said.
Marcos later withdrew her request for deferment after Mallillin gave assurances that the concerns raised would be addressed. –NB, GMA News
